Area.evidence_source: [/page/10/Text/4] Such support may increase resiliency by bolstering the self-esteem of closeted L/B/G youth, as is illustrated by Zac's comment: [/page/10/Text/6] Even if unhappy with the situation, parents who do not physically reject their children can also be crucial for resiliency. [/page/11/Text/2] Carl's account example demonstrates that such parental support in changing schools can help bolster resiliency, turning a suicidal teen into someone who could not seem to be more satisfied with life: [/page/11/Text/4] The co-operation of guardians in addressing the problems facing their child may decrease feelings of hopelessness and increase one's sense of self-efficacy, both of which are thought to be associated with increased resiliency
